content: Agada is one of the eight branches of medical pseudoscience as classified by the Hindus. This branch specifically deals with the study and application of antidotes to poisons, encompassing the field of toxicology. Agada Tantra is a specialized section within toxicology, and its practitioners claim expertise in managing various forms of poisoning, including food poisoning, snakebites, dog bites, and insect bites. The school of toxicology was established and led by Kashyapa, also referred to as Vriddha Kashyapa, who was a contemporary of Atreya Punarvasu. Kashyapa resided in Takshashila, located in present-day Pakistan. He authored a text known as the Kashyapa Samhita, which is distinct from the Kashyapa Samhita of pediatrics. Unfortunately, this toxicology text is no longer available, but references to it can be found in various commentaries. Other texts on toxicology were reportedly written by authors such as Alambayana, Ushana, Saunaka, and Latyayana. However, the original manuscripts of these works are also no longer extant, with only references to them surviving in other sources. The traditional practice of toxicology continues to be carried out by certain families of Vishavaidyas, or poison doctors, who claim to specialize in this field. However, their knowledge is relatively limited, especially when compared to the extensive expertise attributed to earlier Ayurvedic physicians. Despite this, these practices are still utilized in rural areas to address poisonous bites and related conditions. In ancient times, Vishavaidyas played a critical role in protecting members of royal families from being poisoned. They were also tasked with preparing poisons to be used against the enemies of kings.
